title: Endocarditis and Blood Cultures: The 2023 Duke-ISCVID Microbiology Rules
summary: Link the classic organisms of subacute, acute, prosthetic and right-sided endocarditis to the 2023 Duke-ISCVID blood-culture criteria: typical organisms in two sets, nontypical in three, coagulase-negative staphylococci only with prosthetic material, and the Coxiella and PCR routes.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 66 Hit 26 and Ch. 57 Hit 36. Microbiologic criteria from Duke-ISCVID 2023 (Fowler 2023; read via a page-fetch tool); organism patterns from Cuervo 2021 and Shmueli 2020. Hit 36’s “culture-negative subacute = HACEK” is contradicted (register flag rv-hacek-culture; Cuervo 2021: culture-negative IE mostly from prior antibiotics or non-cultivable organisms). Not taught: bone-marrow culture for Brucella and Salmonella Typhi (Hit 36), S. lugdunensis breakpoints, therapy.

objectives: Match endocarditis presentations (subacute native valve, acute, prosthetic/healthcare-associated, right-sided) to their usual organisms.
Apply the 2023 Duke-ISCVID major microbiologic criterion: typical organisms in ≥2 sets, nontypical in ≥3, and the prosthetic-material rule for coagulase-negative staphylococci.
State the Coxiella and PCR routes to a major criterion and the main causes of culture-negative endocarditis.

scenes.title: Three positive bottles
scenes.altText: Invented scenario. Three patients with fever and a new murmur, all with blood cultures drawn before antibiotics: (1) viridans-group streptococcus in 3 of 3 sets, 6 weeks after a dental extraction; (2) coagulase-negative staphylococcus in 1 of 2 sets, native valve, no devices; (3) Staphylococcus aureus in 2 of 2 sets in a person who injects drugs, ill for 3 days. Question token: “Which meet the major blood-culture criterion?”

cues.text: Three patients with fever and a new heart murmur, all with blood cultures taken before antibiotics.

One grows viridans streptococci in three of three sets after dental work. One grows coagulase-negative staphylococci in one of two sets. One grows Staphylococcus aureus in two of two sets after three days of illness.
Which of these meet the major blood-culture criterion for endocarditis?

scenes.title: Who causes endocarditis
scenes.altText: Pattern cards (Cuervo 2021; Shmueli 2020). Classic subacute native-valve endocarditis: viridans-group (oral) streptococci, enterococci and HACEK — the oral-streptococcal “subacute” form, classically linked with rheumatic heart disease, has become less frequent in high-income countries. Acute presentation and/or prosthetic valve: Staphylococcus aureus must be covered. Healthcare-associated trend: older patients, S. aureus, coagulase-negative staphylococci and enterococci, prosthetic valves and cardiac devices. Right-sided endocarditis, most often in people who inject drugs: S. aureus in 60–90% of cases. S. gallolyticus or E. faecalis endocarditis: look for colorectal disease (colonoscopy).

cues.text: The classic slow, subacute endocarditis of a native valve is caused by oral viridans streptococci, enterococci and the HACEK group. It is becoming less common in high-income countries.
An acute, rapidly progressive picture, or a prosthetic valve, points first to Staphylococcus aureus.
Healthcare-associated endocarditis is rising: older patients, staphylococci including coagulase-negative species, enterococci, prosthetic valves and cardiac devices.

In right-sided endocarditis, usually in people who inject drugs, Staphylococcus aureus causes most cases. And Streptococcus gallolyticus or Enterococcus faecalis should prompt a look for bowel disease.

scenes.title: The 2023 Duke-ISCVID blood-culture rules
scenes.altText: Major-criterion card (Duke-ISCVID 2023): TYPICAL organisms in ≥2 separate blood-culture sets — S. aureus, S. lugdunensis, E. faecalis, all streptococci except S. pneumoniae and S. pyogenes, Granulicatella, Abiotrophia, Gemella, HACEK; with intracardiac prosthetic material, also coagulase-negative staphylococci, Corynebacterium, Serratia marcescens, P. aeruginosa, Cutibacterium acnes, non-tuberculous mycobacteria and Candida. NONTYPICAL organisms need ≥3 sets. Coxiella burnetii: one positive culture, or anti-phase I IgG >1:800. PCR or other nucleic-acid test of blood for Coxiella, Bartonella or Tropheryma whipplei. Minor microbiologic criterion: positive cultures that fall short of the major rule. The timing and separate-venipuncture requirements were removed; at least 2 sets should be drawn for suspected bacteraemia. Definite IE (clinical): 2 major, or 1 major + 3 minor, or 5 minor.

cues.text: The 2023 Duke criteria list typical organisms: Staphylococcus aureus and lugdunensis, Enterococcus faecalis, nearly all streptococci except pneumococcus and group A strep, Granulicatella, Abiotrophia, Gemella and HACEK. Two separate positive sets make a major criterion.
Coagulase-negative staphylococci and a few others count as typical only with prosthetic material in the heart. Organisms that rarely cause endocarditis need three or more positive sets.
Coxiella counts as major with one positive culture or a phase one IgG titre above one in eight hundred. PCR of blood for Coxiella, Bartonella or Tropheryma also counts.
The old timing and separate-venipuncture rules were dropped, but at least two sets should be drawn. Definite endocarditis needs two major criteria, one major plus three minor, or five minor.

scenes.title: Score the three patients
scenes.altText: Decision cards. (1) Viridans streptococci in 3/3 sets → typical organism in ≥2 sets: MAJOR criterion met. (2) CoNS in 1/2 sets, native valve, no device → CoNS is not typical without intracardiac prosthetic material, and one set falls short: at most a MINOR criterion, and often a contaminant (see blood-culture contamination lesson). (3) S. aureus in 2/2 sets → MAJOR criterion; acute course in a person who injects drugs fits right-sided S. aureus endocarditis. Culture-negative card: up to 10–20% of IE has no documented organism, mostly because of antibiotics given before cultures, or fastidious and non-cultivable organisms (Coxiella, Bartonella, Tropheryma, Chlamydia); modern automated systems detect HACEK within the standard incubation (see register flag rv-hacek-culture), so HACEK is not the main cause of “culture-negative” IE.

cues.text: Score them. Viridans streptococci in three of three sets: a typical organism in at least two sets. That is a major criterion.
Coagulase-negative staphylococci in one of two sets, on a native valve without a device, is not typical and falls short. At most a minor criterion, and often a skin contaminant.
Staphylococcus aureus in two of two sets is a major criterion. The fast course in a person who injects drugs fits right-sided endocarditis.

And when cultures stay negative, the usual reasons are antibiotics given before cultures, or organisms that grow poorly or not at all, like Coxiella and Bartonella. Modern systems usually grow HACEK in standard time.

props.title: Culture-negative IE (up to 10–20%)
lines: HACEK usually grows in standard time

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards: “Any organism in two sets is a major criterion” (✓ only TYPICAL organisms need two; nontypical organisms need three or more); “CoNS in blood + murmur = endocarditis” (✓ CoNS counts as typical only with intracardiac prosthetic material); “Culture-negative endocarditis = HACEK” (✓ mostly prior antibiotics or non-cultivable organisms such as Coxiella and Bartonella; HACEK usually grows in standard incubation).

cues.text: Trap one: any organism in two sets is a major criterion. No: typical organisms need two sets; others need three or more.
Trap two: coagulase-negative staphylococci plus a murmur means endocarditis. No: they count as typical only with prosthetic material in the heart.
Trap three: culture-negative endocarditis means HACEK. No: it is mostly prior antibiotics, or organisms like Coxiella and Bartonella.

scenes.title: Usual suspects need two witnesses
scenes.altText: Memory aid: “USUAL SUSPECTS need TWO witnesses (two positive sets); STRANGERS need THREE. Skin staph only counts as a suspect if there is HARDWARE in the heart. And Coxiella confesses with ONE culture or a high phase I IgG.” Tokens: typical = 2 sets · nontypical = 3 · CoNS needs hardware. A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: usual suspects need two witnesses, two positive sets. Strangers need three. Skin staphylococci count as suspects only if there is hardware in the heart. And Coxiella confesses with one culture or a high phase one IgG.

Where it breaks: the criteria support, not replace, clinical judgement; they were built for research and classification; imaging and pathology criteria also count; and local guidelines may still use the older Duke version.

explanation.what: Plain language: endocarditis is infection of the heart lining or valves. Doctors use a points system, the Duke criteria; one big point is finding the right kind of germ in more than one blood culture. Which germs count, and how many cultures are needed, depends on how often that germ causes heart-valve infection. Scientific terms: infective endocarditis (IE), viridans-group streptococci, HACEK, coagulase-negative staphylococci (CoNS), Duke-ISCVID 2023 criteria, typical vs nontypical organisms, blood-culture set, Coxiella burnetii phase I IgG, culture-negative IE.
explanation.why: Organisms that commonly cause IE are unlikely to be chance findings when they appear in two sets, whereas skin organisms and rare causes need more evidence. Antibiotics given before cultures, and organisms that do not grow in routine culture, explain most culture-negative cases.
explanation.measure: Major: typical organisms ≥2 separate sets; nontypical ≥3; with intracardiac prosthetic material, CoNS, Corynebacterium, S. marcescens, P. aeruginosa, C. acnes, NTM and Candida are typical; Coxiella one culture or anti-phase I IgG >1:800; blood PCR for Coxiella, Bartonella, T. whipplei. Timing/separate-venipuncture requirements removed; ≥2 sets for suspected bacteraemia. Definite (clinical): 2 major, 1 major + 3 minor, or 5 minor.
explanation.differs: Typical vs nontypical organisms; CoNS with vs without prosthetic material; subacute oral-streptococcal vs acute S. aureus vs healthcare-associated IE; culture-negative from prior antibiotics vs non-cultivable organisms (not HACEK).
explanation.examAngle: Expect: decide whether a set of blood-culture results meets the major criterion, recognise S. aureus in acute or IDU-associated IE, viridans streptococci after dental work, the CoNS prosthetic-material rule, and causes of culture-negative IE.

questions.stem: A patient with a native valve and no intracardiac device has coagulase-negative staphylococci in 1 of 2 blood-culture sets. Under the 2023 Duke-ISCVID criteria, this is:

options.text: Not a major criterion; CoNS is typical only with intracardiac prosthetic material
options.rationale: Correct. Without prosthetic material CoNS is nontypical (≥3 sets needed), and one set falls short.

options.text: A major criterion, because CoNS is a typical organism
options.rationale: Incorrect. CoNS is typical only with intracardiac prosthetic material.
Incorrect. Definite IE needs 2 major, 1 major + 3 minor, or 5 minor criteria.

options.text: Irrelevant because blood cultures do not count in Duke criteria
options.rationale: Incorrect. Blood cultures are central to the microbiologic criteria.

questions.stem: A person who injects drugs has 3 days of high fever and Staphylococcus aureus in 2 of 2 blood-culture sets. Which statement is correct?

options.text: This meets the major microbiologic criterion, and S. aureus is the predominant cause of right-sided IE
options.rationale: Correct. S. aureus is typical; two sets suffice; it causes 60–90% of right-sided IE.

options.text: Three sets are needed because S. aureus is nontypical
options.rationale: Incorrect. S. aureus is a typical organism.

options.text: Viridans streptococci are the most likely cause of acute IE in this setting
options.rationale: Incorrect. Viridans streptococci are associated with subacute native-valve IE.

options.text: The cultures must have been drawn 12 hours apart to count
options.rationale: Incorrect. Duke-ISCVID 2023 removed the timing requirement.

questions.stem: Which is the most common reason for blood-culture-negative endocarditis?

options.text: Antibiotics given before blood cultures were drawn
options.rationale: Correct. Prior antibiotics are the main cause, along with fastidious or non-cultivable organisms such as Coxiella and Bartonella.

options.text: HACEK organisms, which cannot grow in automated systems
options.rationale: Incorrect. Modern automated systems usually detect HACEK within standard incubation.

options.text: Staphylococcus aureus, which grows too slowly
options.rationale: Incorrect. S. aureus grows readily in blood culture.

options.text: Drawing two sets instead of one
options.rationale: Incorrect. At least two sets are recommended.
